mission_1.search: On the open map, the BFS and A* path lengths provided are both 13.5 and expanded-node counts for BFS is 928 and A* is 700. A* examined fewer cells. Both BFS and A* algorithms return the shortest route so the equal path is expected but with the cells they expand there's a slight difference. BFS expands a bit larger than A* because with BFS it expands all around the start counting all its neighbors cells initially then all of the neighbors neighbors and so on, It doesn't know where the goal is so it explores everything evenly like a ripple. popleft() takes out the cell that has been waiting the longest and every new cell that gets appended goes to the back so this just opens all the cells closest to the start first and it'll know the goal has been found whenever the goal itself gets popped. As for A* it uses a heap ordered with heuristics so when it  pops a new cell it updates g and h which indicate the steps taken and the distance left to the goal, if the algorithm see's it's getting closer to the goal it will continue that way, if it see's that it get's further away from the goal then it may not expand that path as there's a shorter heuristic somewhere else. This is the reason why there's fewer expansions, BFS explores all around from the start until it reaches the goal like a ripple, While A* is also a ripple however it's weighted more towards the goal section because it know's where the goal is.
mission_1.failure: The DFS and IDDFS rows covers basically 3x (visually) the amount that the BFS covers on the constrained map,  for expansions DFS is 524, 250001 for IDDFS ,848 for BFS. IDDFS expands 250001 nodes because it does not keep track of the globally visited nodes and explores every path up to it's depth limit over and over again, basically cells can be revisited multiple times so the expansions increase exponentially, For DFS it just explores all the way down a branch until it reaches the goal so the expansion would be way less as it's not looking at everything but it can still take a longer path as it could be exploring a lot of unnecessary cells. BFS once again just explores all neighboring cells around the start and ripples out from that but this one does grab shortest path. For the 4 unreachable-case statuses they basically all could not find a valid path because the S was enclosed in one room and the G was enclosed in another with no valid pathing. The difference between no_path and resource_limit is no_path means that the search was completed but no goal could be found meaning that it was unreachable, whereas resource_limit means the algorithm was stopped before it finished whether it took too long or ran out of expansion budget so it never reached a goal but does not necessarily mean that the goal was unreachable or that there was no goal. Claude was used to help with starting pathing code especially with IDDFS as it was the most confusing however checked that the proper data structures were used and specific cases for each algorithm like iddfs not keeping a global visited, astar stopping when goal is popped.
